motion: This house believes governments should ban new gasoline car sales by 2035

events.text: Welcome to tonight's debate on the motion: this house believes governments should ban new gasoline car sales by 2035. Alex opens for the proposition.
Thank you Sam. The transition is already happening: global electric vehicle sales tripled between 2020 and 2023, according to the International Energy Agency.
In Norway, roughly eighty percent of new cars sold are already electric. A 2035 ban simply confirms where the market is going.
I believe a firm deadline is the fairest policy for both industry and consumers, and I predict most major economies will adopt one within five years.
That optimism ignores the facts. Electric vehicles actually emit more carbon dioxide than gasoline cars over their lifetime, once you count the battery.
And charging infrastructure is a fantasy — you can see the gaps from space, much like the Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon.
Alex, what happens to the used gasoline fleet after 2035 — who pays for stranding millions of working cars?
Jordan's numbers are simply wrong. Lifecycle studies show EVs emit far less CO2 than gasoline cars even including battery manufacturing.
The IEA and the ICCT both confirm this. The evidence is on the proposition's side.
Of course Alex would say that — someone who has never worked a day in the auto industry and clearly doesn't understand real engineering.
In my opinion, mandates are the wrong tool. Markets should decide, not bureaucrats.
Norway shows mandates and markets work together. Unemployment there is at its lowest level in history, even during the transition.
I predict the 2035 targets will quietly slip to 2040 in most countries within two years.
Closing statements please. Thirty seconds each.
The data is clear: EV adoption is accelerating, lifecycle emissions favor electrification, and a 2035 deadline gives industry certainty. Support the motion.
A ban is premature central planning. Vote against the motion and let innovation, not deadlines, decide.
